memory_line: Methotrexate for arthritis: once a week, never every day.
caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift. She's 74 with rheumatoid arthritis, admitted with pneumonia.
• Home: methotrexate 7.5 mg once a WEEK, on Mondays
• Admission order: 7.5 mg DAILY

❌ 3 mistakes
1️⃣ Never compared it with her home list
2️⃣ Kept giving it. "It's only 7.5 mg"
3️⃣ Called her mouth sores thrush and didn't report
➡️ Night 6: her kidneys are slowing, WBC (white blood cells) 0.8, platelets 19, fever, low BP. Rapid response.

🧮 The math
• 6 days × 7.5 mg = 45 mg in 6 days
• That's 6 weeks of methotrexate in 6 days

💊 Methotrexate (ONCE A WEEK)
• For rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis: one dose, one named day a week
• Folic acid is often the daily pill beside it. Don't mix them up
• Too much hits fast-growing cells: bone marrow (infection, bleeding), mouth and gut (sores, diarrhea)
• The kidneys clear it. Kidney trouble makes toxicity worse, faster

✅ The right move
• A daily order for arthritis? Hold it. Clarify with the provider and pharmacy
• Mouth sores, new bruising, fever, diarrhea: report now
• Leucovorin (the rescue drug), as ordered. It works best early

🧠 Methotrexate for arthritis: once a week, never every day.
share_line: 📤 Send this to the nurse who'd give it nightly because it's a low dose.
sources: Methotrexate tablets prescribing information (DailyMed): boxed warning on fatal toxicity from daily instead of weekly dosing
ISMP (Institute for Safe Medication Practices) Targeted Medication Safety Best Practices for Hospitals: weekly oral methotrexate
rn_checks: Oral methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis is dosed once weekly; daily dosing errors have caused fatal toxicity (label boxed warning, ISMP best practice)
Folic acid is commonly given daily alongside it (a known source of mix-ups)
Toxicity: myelosuppression (infection, bleeding), mucositis (mouth sores), diarrhea; report now; leucovorin rescue as ordered, best early

Story: 6 daily doses of 7.5 mg (45 mg) plus pneumonia-related kidney injury (creatinine doubled), then on night 6 WBC 0.8, platelets 19, fever 38.6 °C, BP 84/48. Vera: published daily-dosing cases without kidney injury had milder day-5 counts, so the kidney cause was added. Realistic now?
Leucovorin as soon as possible, as ordered (label)
